title: Visitor-to-first-school commercial journey
problem: A verified purchase must create exactly one tenant and guide its owner to an independent or branched first school without crossing domain or tenant ownership boundaries.
outcomes: A visitor can select an active plan and an authenticated buyer can complete a verified purchase.
A verified subscription provisions exactly one tenant and owner membership.
The tenant owner can create either an independent school or a collection, branch and school hierarchy.
Retries, forged callbacks and cross-tenant identifiers never duplicate effects or disclose another tenant.

personas.exit: one active tenant and owner membership

personas.goal: create the first organization and school

steps.user_result: immutable price and invoice are created
provider redirect or payment instruction is returned
payment is verified server-side and replay-safe
one tenant and owner context are provisioned
the first root or branch organization unit is created
the first school is bound to a same-tenant organization unit
effective capabilities and onboarding completion are displayed

business_rules.rule: Only an active immutable plan version may be checked out.
A provider callback alone never activates a subscription; signature or server inquiry must verify it.
Five deliveries of the same provider event create one provider event, ledger effect, entitlement, subscription activation and tenant.
Tenant provisioning is keyed by subscription_id and is retry-safe.
A tenant owner may create only organization units and schools inside the active tenant context.
Organization parents and school organization units must belong to the same tenant; foreign identifiers return non-disclosing not-found errors.
Organization trees are acyclic and sibling codes are unique within a parent; root codes are unique within a tenant.
Entitlement and permission are evaluated independently before onboarding capabilities are returned.

rules: branch parent is collection in the same tenant
school is bound to a same-tenant branch
moving an org unit requires version and cycle checks

when: checkout and payment attempt are created
the verified event provisions a tenant
the owner creates a root school org unit and school
then: exactly one active subscription and tenant exist
school and org unit share the tenant

given: an active paid tenant owner context
when: the owner creates a same-tenant branch
the owner binds a school to that branch
the identical provider_event_id is delivered five times
then: one ledger effect, entitlement, activation and tenant exist
all repeats return a safe idempotent result

given: an invalid signature and failed provider inquiry
then: no ledger, entitlement, activation or tenant is created

given: an org unit identifier from tenant B
when: the owner uses that identifier as parent
then: tenant B is not disclosed or modified

when: a move would make a node its own ancestor

given: an org unit code already used below a parent
when: the same normalized code is created below that parent

given: an org unit identifier from tenant B
when: the owner tries to bind a school to it
then: tenant B is not disclosed or modified

definition_of_done: Both organization models have executable acceptance scenarios.
Every operation_id exists in the accepted contract and current OpenAPI document.
Every contract acceptance scenario is represented without weakening its expected result or error.
The five-delivery replay produces one financial and provisioning effect.
Ownership boundaries assign every contract-owned table to one writer.
No scenario, event or telemetry field requires card data, child data or secrets.
non_goals: Implementing the backend, database migrations or payment provider adapter
Creating academic years, classes, students or attendance
Changing Nginx, production data or the deployed static preview
